title: Brief special meeting authorizes borrowing and closed session
subtitle: In-camera session on potential litigation, 2026 borrowing by-law and confirming by-law; no delegations
overview: Council held a short special meeting on January 5, 2026, the first of the year. There were no delegations, no declarations of pecuniary interest and no mayoral business.

Council authorized an in-camera meeting to follow, to consider a potential litigation matter under the Municipal Act, 2001 {{vote:m1}}. The minutes report nothing further about that session, so its subject and any outcome are not public from this meeting.

Council also gave third reading to two by-laws. One authorizes the City to borrow for current expenditures in 2026 (By-law 2026-001). The other confirms Council's actions for the day (By-law 2026-002). The minutes record the by-law motion as carried but give no recorded vote. Borrowing authority of this kind lets the City cover day-to-day costs early in the year, before revenues such as taxes arrive. The meeting adjourned at 4:22 p.m.

decisions.detail: Council authorized a closed meeting after the special meeting to consider a potential litigation matter under Section 239(2)(e) of the Municipal Act, 2001 {{vote:m1}}.
Council gave third reading to By-law 2026-001, authorizing borrowing for current expenditures in 2026, along with the confirming by-law.

debate: There was no substantive debate; the chair asked for discussion on the in-camera motion and none was recorded in the transcript.
No delegations were registered, so no residents spoke to any item.
The by-law motion and the motion to adjourn were each put to a voice vote and declared carried without discussion.
